## HIGH IMPACT

### Component: `hui-entities-card` — `hui-section-row` divider selector change

**What changed (`src/panels/lovelace/cards/hui-entities-card.ts`, #55415):**
The CSS selectors that hide the top divider and remove the top margin on the first section row were changed from:

```css
/* OLD */
#states > div:first-child > hui-section-row::part(divider) { display: none; }
#states > div:first-child > hui-section-row::part(label)  { margin-top: 0; }

/* NEW */
#states:first-child > div:first-child > hui-section-row::part(divider) { display: none; }
#states:first-child > div:first-child > hui-section-row::part(label)  { margin-top: 0; }
```

The `:first-child` pseudo-class moved from the `div` to `#states` itself. This means the divider-hiding rule now only fires when `#states` is the first child of its parent, which in practice is nearly always true, but the selector specificity and matching logic has changed.

**Effect on ha-lcars:**
The LCARS theme does not directly inject CSS targeting `hui-section-row::part(divider)` or `hui-section-row::part(label)` in any card-mod rule. However, any LCARS user who has card-mod CSS overriding these `::part()` selectors in their own entities card configurations, or who relies on the divider being visible/invisible for visual layout (LCARS uses section rows as visual dividers inside the entities card border frames), may see the first section row's divider reappear or the label's top margin reapply in edge cases where `#states` is not the first child (e.g., when a card header is present before `#states`).

**Concrete effect:** With a card header present, `#states` is no longer the first child, so the old rule that hid the divider will no longer apply — the top divider on the first section row will now be **visible** when a card header exists. This is a reversal of prior behavior.

**Suggested fix:**
In `card-mod-card` CSS (under entities card rules, particularly `.middle-blank` and any header-bearing entities cards), add an explicit rule to suppress the first section row divider:

```css
:host(.type-entities) ha-card {
  #states > div:first-child > hui-section-row::part(divider) {
    display: none;
  }
  #states > div:first-child > hui-section-row::part(label) {
    margin-top: 0;
  }
}
```

This replicates the old (pre-fix) selector so LCARS-styled entities cards with headers are not affected by the upstream selector scope change.

## MEDIUM IMPACT

### Component: `hui-alert-badge` and `hui-alert-card` — Default color logic change

**What changed (`src/panels/lovelace/badges/hui-alert-badge.ts` and `src/panels/lovelace/cards/hui-alert-card.ts`, #55436):**
`DEFAULT_ALERT_COLOR` (a static fallback color constant) has been replaced by `computeAlertColor` (a function that computes color from entity state). The editor schema (`alert-schema.ts`) now also includes `include_state: true` in the `ui_color` selector for `clear_color`, meaning the color picker now exposes a "state color" option.

The practical result: alert cards and badges that previously fell back to a fixed hardcoded color (`DEFAULT_ALERT_COLOR`) will now receive a **dynamic state-based color** by default. This color is derived from the entity's state and will use HA's standard state color palette — which may conflict with LCARS color overrides.

**Effect on ha-lcars:**
The LCARS theme sets `state-color: var(--lcars-ui-secondary)` (mapped to `--lcars-african-violet`) in `&base`. The new `computeAlertColor` function will use HA's state color system, which reads from `--state-*-color` variables or the tonal palette (`--ha-color-primary-*`). The LCARS theme defines the `ha-color-primary-*` palette (derived from `--lcars-ui-tertiary`, i.e., `--lcars-red`). Alert cards/badges that previously showed a neutral/fixed color will now show a state-derived color that is LCARS-palette-colored (red tones), which may or may not be the desired appearance.

This is not a hard break but will visually change the default appearance of alert card/badge colors that were previously using `DEFAULT_ALERT_COLOR`.

**Suggested fix:**
If the state-color-derived appearance is undesirable for LCARS-styled alert cards, add a card-mod rule targeting `hui-alert-card` and `hui-alert-badge` to force the color:

```css
/* In card-mod-card or card-mod-root */
hui-alert-card ha-card {
  --state-color: var(--lcars-card-button-color);
}
hui-alert-badge {
  --state-color: var(--lcars-card-button-color);
}
```

Alternatively, if the LCARS red-toned state color is acceptable, no fix is needed — but this should be verified visually.

### Component: `hass-tabs-subpage-data-table` — `ha-input-search` min-width change

**What changed (`src/layouts/hass-tabs-subpage-data-table.ts`, layout change):**
A new rule was added to the component's internal shadow DOM styles:

```css
.search-toolbar ha-input-search {
  min-width: 0;
}
```

**Effect on ha-lcars:**
The LCARS theme does not directly style `.search-toolbar ha-input-search` in any card-mod selector. However, the LCARS config page modifications inject CSS into many `hass-tabs-subpage $` contexts (e.g., `"ha-config-automation $ hass-tabs-subpage $"`, etc.). If any of these injections previously relied on `ha-input-search` having an implicit minimum width to establish layout (e.g., affecting how filter chips or toolbar items are positioned relative to the search bar), those layouts could shift.

The `min-width: 0` addition allows the search field to shrink smaller than it previously could, which may change toolbar layout widths in the many config pages the LCARS theme styles.

**Suggested fix:**
Visually inspect the search toolbar in config list pages (Automations, Devices, Entities, Areas, etc.) to confirm the search field and filter chip layout has not visibly shifted. If it has, add to relevant `hass-tabs-subpage $` card-mod blocks:

```css
.search-toolbar ha-input-search {
  min-width: <desired-px-value>;
  /* or flex-grow: 1; to restore full-width expansion */
}
```

### Component: `hui-dialog-add-device-card` and `hui-dialog-suggest-card` — Save success toast removed

**What changed (#55444):**
`showSaveSuccessToast` was removed from both `hui-dialog-add-device-card` and `hui-dialog-suggest-card`. Instead, the toast behavior was moved: `hui-unused-entities` now shows a toast with a link to the dashboard after adding entities. The toast itself (`showSaveSuccessToast` → `showToast` with a link) now navigates to the dashboard.

**Effect on ha-lcars:**
No CSS or visual theme impact. Toast styling is not targeted in the LCARS theme. The toast appearance change (now includes a navigation link) could optionally be themed via `ha-toast` or `ha-snack-bar` selectors if desired, but no existing LCARS rule breaks.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed.
